The Copper Echo

Elias sat in the kitchen, the silence of the 2026 winter pressing against his ears. On the counter, the old baby monitor lay face down, its power cord severed months ago.

A soft crackle emerged from the dead plastic. 'The door is heavy,' a small, familiar voice whispered through the unpowered speaker, vibrating against the cold laminate countertop.

Elias felt the ache of grief turn into a sharp dread as he confirmed the empty battery compartment. 'The door is heavy,' the voice repeated, followed by rhythmic scratching.

He walked to the nursery, his breath hitching, and pushed the door open to find only an empty, dust-covered crib and the oppressive scent of old lavender.

He looked down at the dead monitor; the screen flickered to life, showing a live feed of himself standing in the doorway, filmed from deep inside the floorboards.
